title: Career: telling your work story
theme: Карьера: рассказ о себе и своем опыте
can_do: Рассказать о своем пути: общий итог (I've worked...) и детали с датами (In 2022 I moved...).
Сказать, как долго что-то длится, через for, since и How long...?
Рассказать, чем занимаешься последнее время: I've been working on...
Правильно назвать профессию: I'm a..., I work as an...
Ответить на "Tell me about yourself" на собеседовании IT PM за полторы-две минуты.

points.title: Present perfect or past simple
points.explain_ru: Present perfect (have/has + третья форма) связывает прошлое с сейчас: опыт за всю жизнь (I've managed remote teams), результат, который виден сейчас (We've launched the app, it's live), период, который еще не закончился (this year, so far, today). Как только появляется законченное время (last year, in 2023, two weeks ago, when I was a student) или вопрос When...?, нужен past simple. В рассказе о карьере обычно так: общий итог в present perfect, а детали с датами в past simple. В американском английском с just, already, ever, never часто ставят past simple (I just finished): курс принимает оба варианта, но сам держится британской нормы.

examples.en: I've managed three product launches so far.
examples.ru: На моем счету уже три запуска продукта.

examples.en: We launched the new version last March.
examples.ru: Мы выпустили новую версию в марте прошлого года.

examples.en: Have you ever worked with an outside vendor? Yes, I worked with one at my last job.
examples.ru: Ты когда-нибудь работал с подрядчиком? Да, на прошлой работе.

examples.en: She has just finished the quarterly report.
examples.ru: Она только что закончила квартальный отчет.

examples.en: I haven't had a single day off this month.
examples.ru: В этом месяце у меня не было ни одного выходного.

ru_trap.wrong: We have released the update two weeks ago.
ru_trap.right: We released the update two weeks ago.
ru_trap.why_ru: В русском одно прошедшее время на оба случая. В английском законченная дата (ago, last year, in 2022, yesterday) не уживается с have + третья форма: дата есть, значит past simple.

points.title: Present perfect continuous: what you have been doing
points.explain_ru: have/has been + -ing значит: действие началось в прошлом и идет до сих пор (I've been working here since spring) или только что закончилось, и виден его след (Sorry I'm late, I've been talking to a client). Форма показывает процесс и длительность. Если важны результат или количество (how many, how much), нужен present perfect без -ing: I've written three reports (сколько сделал) против I've been writing reports all morning (чем был занят). Глаголы состояния (know, be, like, have в значении "иметь") остаются без -ing: I've known her for years.

examples.en: I've been working as a product manager for four years.
examples.ru: Я работаю продакт-менеджером четыре года.

examples.en: We've been testing the new checkout since Monday.
examples.ru: Мы тестируем новое оформление заказа с понедельника.

examples.en: You look tired. Have you been working late?
examples.ru: Ты выглядишь уставшим. Задерживался на работе?

examples.en: She's been interviewing candidates all day, so she's exhausted.
examples.ru: Она весь день проводит собеседования, поэтому вымотана.

examples.en: How long have you been leading this team?
examples.ru: Как долго ты руководишь этой командой?

ru_trap.wrong: I work here for three years.
ru_trap.right: I've been working here for three years.
ru_trap.why_ru: По-русски "работаю три года" стоит в настоящем времени. В английском длительность до сейчас (for three years) требует have been + -ing или have + третья форма; настоящее время с for звучит ошибкой.

points.title: for, since, ago and How long...?
points.explain_ru: For + отрезок времени (for three years, for a month, for ages): сколько длится. Since + точка начала (since 2021, since March, since I joined the company): с какого момента. Оба обычно идут с present perfect: I've lived here for two years или since 2024. Вопрос о длительности: How long have you...? Ago устроено иначе: оно отсчитывает назад от сейчас и идет с past simple: I joined two years ago.

ru_trap.wrong: I work at this company since 2022.
ru_trap.right: I've worked at this company since 2022.
ru_trap.why_ru: Русское "работаю с 2022 года" стоит в настоящем. Since в английском требует перфекта: have worked или have been working. Вторая частая ошибка: during three years вместо for three years.

points.title: a / an with jobs: I'm a..., I work as an...
points.explain_ru: Когда говоришь, кем человек работает, перед профессией нужен a или an: she's a designer, he's an engineer. An ставят перед гласным звуком (an analyst, an engineer, an HR manager: "эйч" начинается с гласного звука), a перед согласным звуком (a UX designer: "ю" звучит как "й"). То же после work as и become: I work as a business analyst. Артикля нет во множественном числе (They're developers) и когда должность звучит как титул единственного человека: He became CEO in 2020.

examples.en: I'm a project manager at a logistics company.
examples.ru: Я проектный менеджер в логистической компании.

examples.en: Before that, I worked as an analyst for two years.
examples.ru: До этого я два года работал аналитиком.

examples.en: My sister is an HR manager, and her husband is a UX designer.
examples.ru: Моя сестра HR-менеджер, а ее муж UX-дизайнер.

examples.en: We're looking for an experienced QA engineer.
examples.ru: Мы ищем опытного QA-инженера.

examples.en: She started as a junior developer and became CTO eight years later.
examples.ru: Она начинала младшим разработчиком и через восемь лет стала техническим директором.

ru_trap.why_ru: В русском артиклей нет, поэтому "брат инженер" переносится как есть. В английском профессия одного человека почти всегда идет с a или an. Это одна из самых живучих ошибок русскоязычных, поэтому артикли возвращаются карточкой в каждом юните.

reading.title: From the classroom to the product team
reading.text:
Nadia Haddad has been a product manager for five years, but she didn't start in tech. After university, she worked as a history teacher in a small town. She loved her students, but after three years she felt that she had stopped growing.

In her free time she had been helping a friend's start-up with its online booking system, and she found that she enjoyed it more than marking essays. So she took an evening course in project management and applied for a junior position at a travel company. She didn't get the first job, or the second, but the third employer hired her.

Since then, she has worked on four products and has led two cross-functional teams. Her biggest achievement so far is a mobile app for small hotels, which her team shipped in only five months. "Teaching has helped me more than I expected," she says. "A classroom is a room full of stakeholders. Everyone wants something different, and you have to explain the plan so clearly that they all follow it."

For the last six months, Nadia has been mentoring two people who are switching careers. She tells them the same thing: "Don't hide your background. Explain what you have learned and how it helps the team."

Has she ever regretted leaving the school? "Never," she says with a smile. "But I still check everyone's spelling like a teacher."

listening.title: Working for yourself (Episode 210211, 11 Feb 2021)

questions.q: What is the best job Rob has ever had, and why?
questions.answer: His current job: it is creative and varied, and it is a permanent staff job with a regular income and a pension.

questions.q: What job did Rob once do?
questions.answer: He worked as a paperboy, delivering newspapers.

questions.q: Why do many people work differently now, according to Rob?
questions.answer: Businesses' needs change often, so they need to be agile and change the size and type of their workforce.

questions.q: How did Carla Barker feel about giving up her permanent job?
questions.answer: She found it petrifying and super-scary, and she had doubts about whether she was good enough.

questions.q: Why did Fiona Thomas leave her 9 to 5 job? Give three reasons.
questions.answer: She wanted creative fulfilment, flexibility to look after her mental health, and financial freedom.

questions.q: What was a 'drummer' in the 19th century?
questions.answer: A travelling salesperson who tried to drum up business, that is, increase sales.

key_points: The days of a job for life at one company are gone.
Some people choose to work for themselves; the pandemic forced others into it.
Carla Barker left a permanent job to start a business and found it frightening at first.
Fiona Thomas wanted creative fulfilment, flexibility for her mental health and financial freedom.
Freelancing brings freedom but also risk.
In the 19th century a 'drummer' was a travelling salesperson, not a musician.
